products.name: Grain
products.note: Meeting recording AI; highlight clips; CRM integration; consent and sharing

reading.body:
Grain is a meeting recording platform that captures video, audio, and transcripts from calls and in-person meetings, then uses AI to generate summaries, highlights, and coaching suggestions for sales and customer success teams.

The company's model depends on processing large volumes of meeting data through external AI systems like Claude and ChatGPT. This positions Grain as a data aggregator and conditioning layer for AI inference rather than a compute provider itself. Teams using Grain feed customer calls, sales conversations, and internal discussions into the platform, which then routes the resulting transcripts and video through third-party models. The business scales with adoption across teams, which means more meetings recorded and more inference requests sent downstream.

Grain's stated policy of not using customer data for model training distinguishes it from some competitors but does not eliminate the compute footprint. Every meeting processed still requires inference cycles, storage, and transmission bandwidth. At scale across growing teams, this represents material demand on the grid and data center capacity of the AI providers Grain integrates with.

The data provided covers the company's product category, founding date, location, and regulatory exposure in California, but does not include user numbers, inference volume, or specifics on which AI providers receive the most requests from Grain's platform. These omissions mean the actual compute demand Grain drives remains opaque.

profile_text.body:
Grain is a San Francisco company founded in 2018 that describes itself as an AI notetaker and conversation intelligence platform. According to its site, it records video calls, Slack huddles, and in-person meetings, then produces summaries, account insights, and coaching feedback. It says it captures video, desktop captured audio, and the resulting transcripts and notes, and that meeting data can be delivered to Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI tools. The company says it serves any team that relies on meetings, with a focus on small to mid-market and enterprise sales, customer success, and product teams.

On pricing, Grain says it offers a free plan with unlimited meetings, a 45-minute meeting limit, and 90-day meeting history, while paid plans start at $15/month per user and add advanced AI, conversational intelligence, priority support, unlimited meeting length, and unlimited meeting history. The site states support for over 130 languages for transcription and AI notes, with over 100 additional languages including Arabic, Hebrew, and Thai. Grain also states that neither it nor its subprocessors use customer data for model training, and points to a published subprocessor list.

The company's record here lists a California law exposure count of 236, with no individual cases recorded. No MCP server is listed for it.
